title: U.S. House · New York's 22nd District
area: Central New York, including Syracuse and Onondaga County, plus Madison, Oswego and parts of Oneida County.

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries for this seat were canceled; incumbent John Mannion and Kailee Buller each advanced without appearing on the primary ballot.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he will fight to expand Medicare and Medicaid access, restore the cut ACA tax credits and that there should be a universal public healthcare option.
positions.quote: there should be a universal public healthcare option

positions.summary: Campaign site lists protecting a woman's right to choose, including cosponsoring the Women's Health Protection Act to restore Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: Protecting a Woman’s Right to Choose: Cosponsoring the Women’s Health Protection Act to restore Roe v. Wade and increasing access to reproductive healthcare nationwide.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he supports legislation such as the Enhanced Background Checks Act of 2025 to reform gun laws.
positions.quote: John is supporting legislation like the Enhanced Background Checks Act of 2025 to provide common sense measures to reform our gun laws.

positions.summary: Campaign site says the wealthiest Americans should pay their fair share in taxes.
positions.quote: The wealthiest Americans in the billionaire class should pay their fair share in taxes so the federal government can continue to invest in our communities.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he supports the goals of a transition to renewable energy sources, while keeping energy prices affordable and service reliable.
positions.quote: Supporting the goals of a transition to renewable energy sources using wind, solar, hydroelectric, geothermal, and nuclear energy to power our economy.

positions.summary: Official site says he supported the PUBLIC SAFETY Act, which would redirect the $75 billion in ICE funding from the 2025 budget law to local law enforcement grants, and called for reforms including judicial warrants, no masks and body cameras for immigration agents.
positions.quote: Supported the PUBLIC SAFETY Act that redirects the excessive $75 billion given to ICE from the OBBB and allocates it to local law enforcement grant programs.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets and Rural Development; Conservation, Research and Biotechnology subcommittees) and the Committee on Education and the Workforce in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Kailee Buller
candidates.currentRole: Former Chief of Staff to the Secretary of the U.S. Department of Agriculture

priorities.text: Affordability and jobs, focused on lowering everyday costs such as groceries, gas, childcare and housing.
Energy and utility costs, opposing what she calls Albany's climate mandates and supporting an "all-of-the-above" energy policy.
Agriculture policy, drawing on her USDA experience to focus on cutting regulations and supporting farmers and rural communities.

positions.summary: Supports repealing New York's climate mandates and advancing an "all-of-the-above" energy policy, saying state climate policy has driven up utility costs.
Supports policies that encourage housing development, cut regulations and make it easier for first-time buyers to enter the market.
Her campaign site says she opposes efforts to defund the police and will work to get law enforcement more funding, training and tools.
positions.quote: She will fight to get law enforcement the funding, training, and tools they need to do their jobs effectively and keep our community safe.

statements.quote: We need to make sure that the labor that we bring in is legitimate but also that those who are criminals are out of our country.
statements.context: In a March 2026 CNYCentral interview, reposted on her campaign site

statements.quote: Kailee believes we need practical solutions that expand access to affordable, high-quality childcare and give parents the flexibility they need.
Protect Coverage for Pre-Existing Conditions to ensure coverage can’t be denied or changed because someone got sick.
